name: Prismex
description: A targeted neuro-optic enhancer that specifically boosts the performance of visual augments — optical implants, retinal overlays, and ocular chrome — by flooding the visual cortex's SNT interface with an excitatory peptide compound. Users with augmented eyes experience dramatically expanded visual range: deeper infrared, higher UV sensitivity, greater contrast, and the ability to process visual information at speeds approaching BCI-assisted computation. Users without ocular augments experience vivid, overwhelming synesthetic visual hallucinations.
effects: Augmented visual range expanded across full spectrum simultaneously
Target acquisition and motion tracking in visual augments dramatically accelerated
Low-light and thermal vision augments boosted to near-military performance
Visual detail resolution increased — users describe being able to read text at extreme distances
Unaugmented users: vivid color hallucinations and synesthesia (recreational use)
side_effects: Photosensitivity — bright light becomes painful during effect
Visual augment hardware strain with extended use
Ocular implant overheating in prolonged high-stimulation environments
Unaugmented users: disorientation, inability to navigate during hallucination peak
Rare: visual cortex SNT damage causing permanent color perception alteration
cultural_context: Prismex has two completely different user cultures. Among augmented users — particularly surveillance operatives, snipers, and close-protection detail — it's a tactical tool: taken before a high-risk operation when you need to see everything. Among unaugmented or lightly augmented Tier 2-3 youth, it's an experience drug, dropped at underground visual art events where the synesthetic effects turn music and light into something indescribable. The two communities barely acknowledge each other, but they buy from the same supply chain.
story_hooks: A surveillance operative on Prismex witnessed something they were never meant to see — a meeting, a face, a transaction — and now can't be sure if what they saw was real or a drug-induced artifact. Someone is counting on that uncertainty.

A Tier 2 art collective has been hosting Prismex-fueled sensory events, and the experiences participants describe are too consistent to be random hallucination — someone may be using the drug's visual cortex access to project specific imagery into users' minds

A Novafold distribution hub has been robbed of a significant Prismex shipment — not for street sale, but apparently for bulk tactical use. Someone is equipping a lot of people with augmented vision enhancements for something large
